s2.p: Five miqat stations ring Makkah. Use the one on your route: Dhul Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) coming from Madinah, Al-Juhfah (Rabigh) from the north-west, Qarn al-Manazil (As-Sayl al-Kabir) from Najd and the east, Yalamlam from Yemen, and Dhat Irq from Iraq. If you are flying, enter ihram before the plane passes over the miqat; crew usually announce it.
foot.p: This guide follows widely accepted practice. Some details differ between schools of thought, such as the prayer before ihram or whether shortening must cover the whole head, so check points that matter to you with a scholar or your group leader.
s2.forbidden: cutting hair or nails, perfume, hunting, marital relations and marriage contracts. Men may not cover the head or wear stitched clothing; women may not wear niqab or gloves.
s3.li3: Start in line with the Black Stone. Face it, raise your right hand and say the takbir. Kiss or touch it if you can reach it easily; otherwise simply point.
s1.li3: Men wear two plain, unstitched white sheets: the izar around the waist and the rida over the shoulders, with sandals that leave the ankles uncovered.
heroLede: Six rites, walked through one at a time with moving diagrams, so you know where to stand, which way to turn and what to say before you arrive.
s3.tr2: Between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone: "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the Fire."
s6.li1: Men either shave the whole head (halq), which carries more reward, or shorten the hair evenly from all over the head (taqsir).
s3.li6: Touch the Yemeni corner if you can, without pointing to it. There is no set du'a for each circuit: pray in any language.
s1.li4: Women wear ordinary loose, modest clothing of any colour, keeping the face and hands uncovered (no niqab or gloves).
s1.note: Wearing the clothes alone does not put you in ihram. That happens with the intention at the miqat, the next step.
s4.li2: Pray two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim if there is space. If it is crowded, anywhere in the mosque is valid.
s3.li4: Walk counterclockwise with the Kaaba on your left, passing outside Hijr Ismail, the low semicircular wall.
s5.li2: Walk to Marwah. That is one lap. Returning to Safa is the second. You finish the seventh lap at Marwah.
s1.svg: Ghusl, then the two white sheets of ihram: the rida over the shoulders and the izar around the waist
s3.li2: Men uncover the right shoulder by passing the rida under the right arm (idtiba) for the whole tawaf.
s5.tr1: "Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah" (2:158). Recite once, when first approaching Safa.
s6.li2: Women gather their hair and cut about a fingertip's length (around 2 cm) from the ends, in private.
s4.tr1: "And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer" (2:125), recited as you approach the Maqam.
s4.svg: Pilgrim moving from the mataf to pray behind Maqam Ibrahim, then a cup filling with Zamzam water
s4.li3: It is sunnah to recite Surah al-Kafirun in the first rak'ah and Surah al-Ikhlas in the second.
s3.li5: Men walk briskly with short steps (ramal) in the first three circuits, then at a normal pace.
s5.li5: Wudu is recommended but not required for sa'i. Wheelchairs are available on the upper floors.
s3.svg: Animated tawaf: seven counterclockwise circuits around the Kaaba starting at the Black Stone
s3.li1: Be in wudu. Enter the mosque with your right foot and stop the talbiyah when tawaf begins.
s5.svg: Animated sa'i: seven laps between Safa and Marwah, with a green-lit section in the middle
s5.li3: Men jog lightly between the two green lights; women walk at a normal pace throughout.
s2.svg: Map of the five miqat stations around Makkah with a plane crossing the boundary
s2.tr2: The talbiyah. Men recite it aloud, women quietly, often, until you begin tawaf.
s4.li4: Drink Zamzam water and make du'a. It is found in coolers throughout the mosque.
s1.li5: If it is not a prayer time, many pray two rak'ahs before entering ihram.
s6.p: With this, your Umrah is complete and every ihram restriction is lifted.
s5.li4: At Marwah, face the Kaaba and repeat the du'a, as you do at each hill.
s4.caption: Cover your right shoulder, pray behind the Maqam, then drink Zamzam.
s1.li1: Trim nails, remove unwanted body hair and take a full bath (ghusl).
s5.tr2: On Safa and Marwah, facing the Kaaba, followed by your own du'a.
heroSvg: Top-down view of pilgrims circling the Kaaba counterclockwise
s1.caption: Bathe, then put on ihram clothing before you reach the miqat.
s4.li1: Men cover the right shoulder again; idtiba is only for tawaf.
s1.li2: Men may apply perfume to the body, not to the ihram clothes.
s5.li1: Climb Safa, face the Kaaba, raise your hands and make du'a.
s2.tr1: Here I am, O Allah, for Umrah. Say this as your intention.
s6.where: Right after sa'i, at the barbers near Marwah or your hotel
s6.caption: Shave or shorten the hair to leave the state of ihram.
s1.where: At home, your hotel, or the airport before departure
s3.tr1: At the Black Stone, at the start of each circuit.
s5.where: Seven laps between the hills of Safa and Marwah
